$comment: An AAR has ONE `assets/` tree and no per-ABI variant of it, so the typelibs this plugin
ships are taken from a single declared source ABI and used by every ABI in the APK. That
is only sound while the typelibs are ABI-neutral, and `.typelib` blobs are NOT neutral in
general: they record struct sizes and field offsets.
MEASURED on the arm64-v8a and x86_64 trees this bundle is built from: 20 of the 21 typelibs
are BYTE-IDENTICAL across the two ABIs — including Gio-2.0 and GObject-2.0, which describe
hundreds of structs. Both ABIs are 64-bit little-endian with the same alignment rules, so
no offset differs. The 21st is listed below.
The build therefore compares every typelib across every requested ABI and FAILS BY NAME on
a divergence that is not declared here. A real offset difference — a 32-bit ABI, say — would
be red rather than a shared asset tree quietly describing the wrong layout.

divergent.reason: x86_64 introspects one extra constant, VA_COPY_AS_ARRAY, which arm64-v8a's va_copy does not produce. Measured: the x86_64 blob's string pool is a strict superset of arm64-v8a's by exactly that one name (230,648 vs 230,588 bytes); no other string differs in either direction. Shipping the arm64-v8a blob therefore omits GLib.VA_COPY_AS_ARRAY from introspection on x86_64 — a constant absent, never a wrong layout — and nothing in @gjsify reads it.
